name: Córdoba
title: Holidays in Córdoba
intro: A Moorish city on the Guadalquivir, home to the extraordinary Mezquita mosque-cathedral and courtyards overflowing with flowers. Here's what Córdoba is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The Roman bridge over the Guadalquivir in Córdoba, with the Mezquita behind
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: March to May and October are ideal, with the patio festival and spring fair in May. July and August are among the hottest in Europe, often near 40°C. Winter is cool and sunny, with fewer visitors.

things.name: Mezquita
things.blurb: A forest of red-and-white arches in a former mosque with a cathedral built inside. Free early-morning entry on most days.

things.name: Alcázar de los Reyes Cristianos
things.blurb: A fortress with terraced gardens and fountains.

things.name: Roman Bridge
things.blurb: Walk across the river at sunset for the view back to the Mezquita.

things.name: Patios
things.blurb: Flower-filled courtyards, at their best during the May festival.

things.name: Judería
things.blurb: The old Jewish quarter of narrow white lanes and a medieval synagogue.

things.name: Medina Azahara
things.blurb: Ruins of a 10th-century palace city, just outside town.

faqs.question: Is Córdoba worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Mezquita is one of the most remarkable buildings in Europe, and the old town is easy to explore in a day or two.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Córdoba?
faqs.answer: One or two days. Many people combine it with Seville and Granada for a week.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Córdoba?
faqs.answer: March to May and October, around 21 to 28°C. Summer is extremely hot.

faqs.question: How do you get to Córdoba?
faqs.answer: Fly into Seville or Málaga, both with direct flights from the UK, then take the fast train, about 45 minutes to an hour.

faqs.question: When is the Córdoba patio festival?
faqs.answer: Usually in the first half of May, when families open their flower-filled courtyards to visitors.
